name: TeleMem

paper.title: TeleMem: Building Long-Term and Multimodal Memory for Agentic AI

construction.unit: event summary per dialogue round + one sentence per character per round
construction.kept_as: LLM summaries (20-100 characters per round) and per-character extractions; raw turns kept alongside but not read
construction.processing: per round (a turn and its reply, with the 3 earlier rounds as context) the LLM writes an event summary and one sentence for each of the two characters; event summaries are batched, matched to near-duplicates, clustered and deduplicated by the LLM

organization.structure: event store linked into a DAG (edges between similar events, oriented by time) + two per-character stores
organization.stores: per conversation: FAISS indexes for events, character A and character B; a graph JSON over events
organization.index: dense (Qwen3-8B embedding, FAISS inner product on normalised vectors)

management.operations: paper: add / update / delete / no-op per cluster, Insert and ReInsert of edges, tombstone deletes; code: the LLM keeps or drops new event summaries per cluster and the kept ones are appended
management.conflicts: LLM consolidation over clusters of summaries with cosine ≥ 0.95

retrieval.candidates: top-10 events by embedding (seeds) and top-10 from each character store
retrieval.selection: closure: every earlier event linked to a seed (up to 100 steps), sorted by timestamp and deduplicated; no reranker
retrieval.budget: 10 seeds + all their ancestors (no count cap) + 10 + 10 character sentences

use.context: event summaries in time order, then character sentences, pasted as one 'material' block before the question
use.reasoning: single answer call for text; a ReAct loop (retrieval, rag, clip QA) for video

classify.note: Dense top-10 seeds, then every earlier event linked to them is added; nothing reranks or filters the closure. Character sentences come from a separate dense top-10.

stages.ingestion: The dialogue is split into rounds (a turn and the reply); each round is processed with the three earlier rounds as context, 16 rounds in parallel.
stages.construction: Per round the LLM writes an event summary of 20-100 characters and one sentence about each of the two characters (relations, events, traits, objects); each is embedded.
stages.organization: Events go to a per-conversation FAISS index and are later linked into a graph: an edge joins events with cosine ≥ 0.9 (at most 5 per node), directed from later to earlier, and a shortcut a→c is dropped when a→b→c exists. Character sentences go to two separate FAISS stores.
stages.update: Each new event pulls stored events with cosine ≥ 0.95 (top 10); after 64 buffered events the pool is clustered (≥ 0.95) and an LLM keeps or drops the new summaries per cluster. The paper's online ReInsert and tombstone deletion are not in the code.
stages.retrieval: The question's top-10 events are seeds; every earlier event reachable through graph edges (≤ 100 steps) joins, sorted by timestamp and deduplicated; top-10 sentences from each character store are appended.
stages.answer: Qwen3-8B (no-think, temperature 0) reads the joined text as material and outputs one option letter on ZH-4O.

summary: Per-round event summaries and per-character notes are batch-deduplicated by an LLM, linked into a time-ordered graph of similar events, and read by taking the question's best-matching events together with every earlier event they link to.
notes:
AXES-CHECK: candidates = graph walk (dense seeds, then backward closure over similarity edges); management = consolidate in the paper, but the code only keeps or drops new summaries and never updates or removes a stored entry. Venue: arXiv preprint (v4, 22 Jan 2026); no venue stated. Code pinned at cdc2cb32 (2026-01-16), the last commit before v4; it adds the ZH-4O evaluation (baselines/telemem).
DESIGN: §3.1-3.3, §4, App. A; code telemem/main.py, telemem/utils.py, baselines/telemem/EvalModel.py and config.yaml. The multimodal module (video to event/object memories, ReAct QA) is described in §3.3.2 but has no reported experiment.

sources.code_note: Official repo linked on the paper's first page. Pinned at cdc2cb32 (2026-01-16, 'eval_telemem'), the last commit before arXiv v4 (2026-01-22); it adds the ZH-4O evaluation script used here. Later commits (from 2026-05) remove the vendored mem0 and move this variant out of the package. No LoCoMo evaluation script for TeleMem is in the repo at this commit.

headline: The answer model reads short LLM summaries only: an event line per round plus character sentences, never the dialogue.
The 'causal' graph is built from embedding similarity (cos ≥ 0.9) and the processing time of each summary, not from dependencies stated in the dialogue.
Every earlier event linked to a seed joins the context, with no cap on the count.

discussion.takeaway: Summarise every round into short event and character notes, deduplicate them in batches, and at question time add every earlier event linked to the best matches. It is best on the Chinese role-play benchmark ZH-4O but trails full context on LoCoMo.

claims.claim: TeleMem is the most accurate method on ZH-4O.
It beats Mem0 by 19% in accuracy with 43% fewer tokens and a 2.1× speedup.
claims.evidence: Abstract. The accuracy gap is 16.13 points (86.33 vs 70.20); no table or setup is given for tokens or speed.

claims.claim: Both the write and the read model matter, and they should be scaled together.
claims.evidence: Accuracy 52.72 with 0.6B writer and reader, 86.33 with 8B/8B, best 87.55 with 14B/14B. Table 2

claims.claim: On LoCoMo it is strong on single-hop and temporal questions but weak on multi-hop.
claims.evidence: Single-hop 64.53, temporal 78.47, multi-hop 20.56; overall 61.49 vs 70.71 for long context and 57.59 for Memobase. Table 3, §4.2

limits: Weaker on multi-hop questions over stored memories (LoCoMo).
The closure can grow large; the paper suggests bounding depth or budgeted expansion.
reading: There is no ablation: no run removes the graph closure or the character stores, so what the DAG adds to 86.33 is untested.
The graph comes from embedding similarity (cos ≥ 0.9) and processing order, not from causal links in the dialogue; edges point from later to earlier by timestamp.

Timestamps are the wall-clock time a summary was written or consolidated, and rounds are summarised on 16 threads, so 'chronological' order in the answer context follows processing rather than the dialogue.
The code never updates or deletes a stored entry: consolidation only keeps or drops new summaries, and the online Insert / ReInsert / tombstone steps of §3.2.3 are absent.
The answer context mixes the graph closure with a plain dense top-10 from each character store; the ZH-4O score cannot separate the two.
The LoCoMo run has no code in the repo, the extraction prompts are Chinese, and TeleMem's multi-hop score (20.56) is below RAG (32.39); the LoCoMo setup (judge prompt, answer prompt) is not given.
The '19%' matches (86.33 − 70.20) / 86.33, i.e. relative to TeleMem's own score; relative to Mem0 the gain is 23%.
Table 2 is not monotonic in the reader as the text says: a 32B reader scores below 8B and 14B readers for 8B, 14B and 32B writers.
ZH-4O is multiple choice, so chance level is above zero; LoCoMo drops the adversarial category (1,540 questions).

abstract.text: TeleMem builds long-term memory for agents as threads of events rather than isolated snippets. Dialogue rounds are summarised into event notes and per-character notes; new notes are batched, matched to similar stored ones, clustered and consolidated by an LLM before storage. Events are linked into a time-ordered graph, and a question retrieves its closest events together with the earlier events they depend on. A multimodal module turns video into event and object memories read by a ReAct-style agent. The authors report higher accuracy than Mem0 on the ZH-4O role-play benchmark with fewer tokens and faster processing.
